title: Word Abbreviation
summary: Given an array of distinct strings, return the minimal possible abbreviations for each word.
statement: Given an array of distinct strings, return the minimal possible abbreviations for each word. The abbreviation starts with the first character, followed by the count of characters in between, and ends with the last character. If multiple words share the same abbreviation, increment the prefix length until all abbreviations are unique. If an abbreviation is not shorter than the original word, return the original word.
constraints: 1 <= len(words) <= 400; 2 <= word length <= 400; distinct lowercase English words.
Start with first letter + omitted-character count + last letter. Increase the prefix of EVERY colliding abbreviation until results are unique.
Return results in input order. Keep a word unchanged if its abbreviation would not be strictly shorter.
hints: Only words with equal length and final letter can collide at an equal prefix length.
Build a prefix trie per length/final-letter group and count words passing through each node.
For each word, walk until a node has count one. Use that prefix, the remaining internal count, and last letter; keep the original if no length is saved.
A group key must include length and final letter. Use original input order for output, and expand all members of a collision group conceptually.
editorial: Within a fixed length/final-letter group, a prefix is unique exactly when its trie node belongs to one word. The first such prefix is precisely where the repeated collision-expansion process stops. Different groups cannot collide because the omitted count and final letter distinguish them. Construct and query the tries in O(S) time and space for S total input characters, then enforce strict shortening. An independent oracle directly simulates simultaneous abbreviation collisions instead of using a trie.

tests.explanation: like becomes l2e, while internal and interval need prefixes so long that their original words are retained. intension and intrusion separate at inte4n and intr4n. Preserve input order.
Both start as a4f, then both become ab3f. Their next prefixes differ, producing abc2f and abn2f; extending just one colliding word is not allowed.
